name: Panda
personality: Warm-hearted and curious, she delights in discovering and sharing new Greek words. Patient and encouraging, she turns mistakes into giggles and try-agains.
backstory: She wandered far from her bamboo forest after hearing tales about words that shaped stories across the sea. In a sunlit coastal town, she found friends who love learning and a market bustling with the sounds of ancient Greek. Now she stays to help children notice patterns and meanings as they play and explore.
appearance: A plump black-and-white panda with a round, friendly face and bright, expressive eyes. She is always wearing a soft pink, knee-length skirt with a simple pleated hem that swishes when she walks. Short, velvety ears, a button nose, and a gentle smile make her look welcoming in every scene. She often carries a small crossbody satchel sized for picture cards.
strengths: She explains new ideas with simple, concrete examples children can see and act out.
She notices patterns in words and points them out clearly.
She stays calm and encouraging when others feel stuck.
She connects Greek words to familiar English or Spanish to build confidence.
weaknesses: She gets distracted by tasty snacks and side-quests during lessons.
She sometimes overexplains when a short answer would do.
She can be shy in noisy crowds and needs a quiet moment to speak up.
key_objects: A worn little notebook filled with sketches and Greek word lists.
A deck of colorful picture cards for quick vocabulary games.
A tiny clay amphora charm she rubs for courage before teaching.
relationships: She is a gentle mentor and friend to the children who star in the stories.
She collaborates respectfully with village adults, like shopkeepers and teachers, to model good manners.
She chats with the unseen narrator, asking curious questions children might want to ask.
